1.meaningHtml: A matrix whose rows are weighted averaging instructions: entries are nonnegative and each row sums to one.

The set of single complex numbers that can occur as eigenvalues of some stochastic matrix with <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> rows.
The hull contains all weighted averages of the given points. A vertex cannot be obtained by averaging other points of the hull.

A polygon satisfying <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mi>P</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda P\subseteq P</annotation></semantics></math>: rotating and scaling any point of <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> keeps it in <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math>.
A line touching the polygon while all its points lie on one side of that line.

<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>w</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mi>/</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_j=(w-\beta_j)/(1-\beta_j)</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mi>q</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w=z^q=a+ib</annotation></semantics></math> and <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b>0</annotation></semantics></math>. Normalisation preserves its argument. Here <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a,b</annotation></semantics></math> are the real and imaginary parts of <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>w</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mi>/</mi><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=(1-a)/b</annotation></semantics></math> and every factor obeys <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Re</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Im</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{Re}g_j+c\operatorname{Im}g_j=1</annotation></semantics></math>. At argument <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math>, its modulus is <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/(\cos u+c\sin u)</annotation></semantics></math>.

A new order-<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> fraction appears in an old interval exactly when <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b+d=n</annotation></semantics></math>.
The left side of the new scalar equation minus its right side. A negative residual at the old radius puts the new root farther out.

The proof establishes <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{n-1}(\theta)\le K_n(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> before identifying either candidate with the actual boundary; nesting of the regions alone would not prove this.

Topic XII identifies <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_n=K_n</annotation></semantics></math> for <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\ge4</annotation></semantics></math>; order three needs a separate negative-ray check.

Compactness ensures that the maximum is attained.

12.termHtml: Requested order <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> and least realising order <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>
12.meaningHtml: <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> is the smallest matrix order realising the selected maximiser; <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\le n</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\ge4</annotation></semantics></math>, its geometric product uses <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">⌊</mo><mi>k</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">⌋</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m=\lfloor k/q\rfloor</annotation></semantics></math>, while the order-<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> scalar candidate uses <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">⌊</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">⌋</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lfloor n/q\rfloor</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta_3</annotation></semantics></math> is the triangle with vertices <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> and the two cubic roots of unity, together with the real segment <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">[</mo><mi>−</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>−</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1,-1/2]</annotation></semantics></math>. The negative-ray maximum is one, although the nearby nonreal radii tend to <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/2</annotation></semantics></math>.

At a point of radius <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo><</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r<K_n(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>, the gap <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_n(\theta)-r</annotation></semantics></math> is positive. Continuity keeps that gap positive nearby, proving the point is interior.

For a maximiser with <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\ge4</annotation></semantics></math>, the proof combines <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_n(\theta)\le K_k(\theta)\le K_n(\theta)\le R_n(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>. The small-order cases are checked separately.

13.meaningHtml: For this budget, <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">⌊</mo><mi>N</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">⌋</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m=\lfloor N/q\rfloor</annotation></semantics></math>, <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A=2\pi t/s</annotation></semantics></math> and <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mi>/</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B=2\pi(1-t)/(mq)</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0<t<1</annotation></semantics></math> in the oriented Farey interval.

<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">inf</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">{</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn><mo>:</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_P(x)=\inf\{a>0:x\in aP\}</annotation></semantics></math>. An asymmetric polygon can have <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>−</mi><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_P(-x)\ne V_P(x)</annotation></semantics></math>, so its gauge need not be a norm.

The smallest <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> for which <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi>P</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mi>γ</mi><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho R_\theta P\subseteq\gamma P</annotation></semantics></math> among convex polygons with at most <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> vertices and zero in their interior. The exact optimum is <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mi>/</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_N=\rho/K_N(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>.

In the coordinate calculation the letter <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is reused locally for the angle <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mi>/</mi><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi/7</annotation></semantics></math>.

14.meaningHtml: In the coordinate and convexity calculation, <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is an angle, not the record time. The selected <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> satisfies <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho^3(1+\rho)=2\cos h</annotation></semantics></math>.

14.meaningHtml: <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mi>/</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=\rho/(1+\rho)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=1/(1+\rho)</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha+\beta=1</annotation></semantics></math>. The two interior contacts use these same weights.

14.meaningHtml: For this polygon, <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi_{i+8}=\Phi_i+2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>.
